title: Early midazolam exposure and short-term risk of acute exacerbation of COPD in critically ill patients: a target trial emulation using the MIMIC-IV database.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sedation is frequently required in the intensive care unit (ICU), but benzodiazepines may worsen respiratory outcomes in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether early midazolam exposure after ICU admission is associated with the short-term risk of acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) among critically ill COPD patients. METHODS: Using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database, we emulated a target trial and applied a clone-censor-weight (CCW) approach to address immortal time bias and informative censoring. Exposure was midazolam administration within a grace period after ICU admission (primary: 24 h; sensitivity: 12 and 36 h). The primary outcome was AECOPD, defined as initiation of systemic corticosteroids or antibiotics between 24 h and 7 days after ICU admission. Outcomes were compared using inverse probability of censoring weights (IPCW). RESULTS: Among 3,416 ICU stays, 233 (6.8%) received midazolam within 24 h. After IPCW weighting, AECOPD incidence was 29.8% in the midazolam group versus 23.5% in controls (risk difference +6.3%, 95% CI -2.7% to +15.8%; odds ratio 1.38, 95% CI 0.86-2.12; p = 0.158). Findings were directionally consistent across grace periods (12 h OR 1.64; 36 h OR 1.29), but none of the grace-period comparisons reached statistical significance. CONCLUSION: In the primary 24 h analysis, early midazolam exposure was associated with a numerically higher short-term AECOPD risk. These observational findings cannot establish causality, and the present study did not demonstrate a statistically significant causal effect; nevertheless, in view of existing ICU sedation evidence, continued caution in the use of midazolam in critically ill COPD patients appears prudent.

title: Target Trial Emulation or Target Trial Approximation?
abstract: Target trial emulation has contributed to improvements in the design and interpretation of observational studies aimed at causal inference. By encouraging researchers to think explicitly about the design of a hypothetical randomized trial, it has helped identify and address avoidable design flaws. However, the framework cannot overcome biases and limitations inherent in observational data. Despite the aim of emulating a randomized trial, observational data cannot reproduce random treatment assignment or blinding, and may not necessarily provide greater generalizability than a randomized trial. Thus, the term "emulation" may imply a degree of similarity to a randomized trial that observational data cannot realistically achieve and deserves critical reconsideration to better reflect the limitations of observational data.

title: A 6-8-Hour Nighttime Sleep Strategy and Subsequent Cognitive Performance: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Sleep duration is a modifiable factor linked to cognitive aging among middle-aged and older adults, but existing evidence is largely correlational. Using observational data in which sleep duration was self-reported, we emulated a target trial to estimate the effect of maintaining a 6-8 h nighttime sleep strategy on subsequent cognitive performance. METHODS: This target trial emulation study analyzed participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), a longitudinal, nationally representative prospective cohort of Chinese adults aged 45 years and older, and followed them from 2011 to 2020. Nocturnal sleep duration was self-reported at every wave. The 6-8 h sleep strategy was compared with a non-6-8 h strategy (<6h or >8h) using intention-to-treat (ITT), per-protocol (PP), and inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW)-weighted PP analyses. Primary outcome was the total cognitive score (range 0-21) after 9 years. Groups were balanced by 1:1 propensity-score matching (PSM) on 18 baseline covariates, and missing baseline covariate data were handled by multiple imputation by chained equations. RESULTS: Of 8147 eligible participants, 2341 matched pairs were included after PSM. The 6-8 h sleep strategy was consistently associated with higher cognitive scores than the non-6-8 h strategy in the ITT analysis (β = 0.237, 95% CI 0.016 to 0.458, p=0.036), the unweighted PP analysis (β = 0.394, 95% CI -0.013 to 0.801, p=0.058), and the IPCW-weighted PP analysis (β = 0.614, 95% CI 0.176 to 1.052, p=0.006). All estimates were modest in absolute terms, corresponding to 5.3% and 13.7% of one standard deviation of the outcome for the ITT and weighted PP analyses. The dose-response curve showed a nonlinear, inverted U-shaped association (P for non-linearity <0.001), with the highest predicted cognition at about 6.7 h of sleep. Neither sex nor age modified the association (P for interaction 0.84 and 0.27). CONCLUSION: By emulating a target trial with repeated prospective cohort data, this study moves beyond simple association and suggests that maintaining 6-8 h of self-reported nighttime sleep is associated with modestly higher subsequent cognitive performance. Target trial emulation improves the rigour of effect estimation but does not eliminate residual confounding, exposure misclassification or selective attrition; the findings require confirmation in studies using objective sleep assessment and more complete control of time-varying confounding.

title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. METHODS: Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. RESULTS: In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; p = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. CONCLUSION: JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

title: Key considerations in the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of observational studies in dialysis.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: In this review, key considerations in the design, conduct, and analysis of observational studies in dialysis research are explored in a unique patient population for which interventional trials are challenging and limited. RECENT FINDINGS: The use of target trial emulation is increasing and provides a conceptual framework for the design of observational studies. A target trial is a hypothetical trial that would be conducted to answer a research question. It requires investigators to ask a clinically relevant question and then specify eligibility criteria, the treatment strategies that will be compared, the follow-up period, outcomes of interest, and the causal contrast (intention-to-treat vs. per-protocol analysis). The protocol for an observational study is then created to mirror the target trial. In doing so, the question is clear, bias is reduced, and underlying assumptions are made transparent. Illustrative examples are used to highlight common pitfalls in dialysis research. SUMMARY: In conclusion, randomized controlled trials are not always feasible or even the ideal approach for answering certain questions. However, observational studies are challenging and require careful planning and execution to ensure robust, unbiased results. Target trial emulation provides a blueprint to improve the quality of observational study design.

title: Propensity Score Methods and Target Trial Emulation in Orthopaedic Surgery: A Practical Guide to Causal Inference from Observational Data.
abstract: » The propensity score is a patient's modeled probability of receiving a treatment given measured baseline characteristics (covariates). Matching patients with similar scores balances those covariates between groups, approximating the comparability achieved by randomization. » Target trial emulation specifies the protocol of the ideal randomized trial and then reproduces it in observational data, enforcing an explicit eligibility window, time zero (the single point at which eligibility, treatment assignment, and the start of follow-up coincide), and analysis plan. » Regression adjusts for confounders within the outcome model, whereas propensity score matching balances those confounders before outcomes are examined. Propensity matching is preferred for rare outcomes or many confounders, where regression tends to overfit. » Neither propensity matching nor target trial emulation addresses unmeasured confounding, and both lose validity in small single-center cohorts with limited overlap (few treated and untreated patients who resemble one another closely enough to be fairly compared); a randomized trial remains the reference standard when feasible. » When appraising studies using propensity matching or target trial emulation, look for 3 key features: (1) Postmatching covariate balance: Are the treatment groups well balanced after matching? (standardized mean difference <0.10). (2) Positivity: Is there enough overlap in patient characteristics that treated and untreated patients can be fairly compared? (3) Unambiguous "time zero": Did follow-up begin at the same well-defined starting point for all patients?

title: [Target trial emulation in acupuncture-moxibustion clinical research: from real-world data to causal inference].
abstract: In order to elucidate the application value and implementation pathway of target trial emulation (TTE) in clinical research of acupuncture and moxibustion, this article reviews the key methodological components of TTE, including data readiness assessment, target trial protocol specification, treatment strategy allocation, alignment of time zero (T0), definition of outcomes and follow-up, estimation-based target choice, control of confounding and censoring, diagnostic and sensitivity analyses, and reporting standards. Key operational points are also summarized based on real-world study (RWS) cases of acupuncture and moxibustion. Using a hypothetical randomized controlled trial (RCT) as the reference, TTE translates a research question into an executable observational study protocol, thereby helping to address pre-control design bias, enhance research transparency and strengthen causal interpretation. The application of TTE in acupuncture- moxibustion research should rely on standardized case registration system and emphasize the structured collection of real-world data. Findings from TTE studies may serve as an important complement to RCT evidence, but they remain the limitations such as data quality, unmeasured confounding factors, and the difficulty in simulating sham-acupuncture controls. Hence, these findings should be interpreted and applied with caution.

title: A primer on target trial emulation for respiratory research.
A study using the REIN registry suggests a statin therapy benefits for secondary prevention in patients receiving dialysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: While statins are effective for cardiovascular prevention in the general population, their benefit in patients with CKD G5D (kidney failure treated by dialysis) remains uncertain. Previous randomized controlled trials included mixed populations for primary and secondary prevention while excluding patients with recent cardiovascular events, leaving a knowledge gap regarding statin effectiveness for secondary prevention immediately following an atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event. Here, we address this gap by providing real-world evidence. METHODS: We conducted a landmark-based observational study, informed by the target trial framework using the French Renal Epidemiology and Information Network (REIN) registry and merged with data from the French national healthcare system database from 2010 to 2023. We included adults with CKD G5D who experienced an ASCVD event. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance baseline characteristics between statin initiators and non-initiators, thereby estimating the average causal effect on all-cause mortality. Results focus on the relative and absolute risk difference and the life expectancy gain using delta restricted mean survival time (dRMST). RESULTS: The study cohort included 5534 patients (median age: 75 years; 67% male). During the ten years of follow-up, statin use was associated with a reduced risk of mortality. The survival curves reached a maximum absolute difference at year four (risk difference -6.2% (95% CI: -10.2; -2.2); relative risk 0.88 [95% CI: 0.81; 0.96]). Life expectancy extended significantly over time with a mean survival gain of 69 days at five years (95% CI: 14-125) and reaching 135 days at ten years (95% CI: 31-239). No difference was identified between groups regarding hospitalizations for rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis. CONCLUSIONS: In patients receiving dialysis, statin initiation following an ASCVD event is safe and associated with a modest-to-moderate ten-year cumulative survival benefit. While interpreted within observational limitations, this real-world evidence supports their use in this secondary prevention setting.

title: Active Surveillance for Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia: Are We Ready for Surgical De-escalation?
abstract: Atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) remains one of the few benign breast lesions for which surgical excision is routinely recommended because of the risk of underlying carcinoma, most commonly ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). However, increasing interest in active surveillance has emerged alongside broader trends toward surgical de-escalation and ongoing prospective trials evaluating observation for low-risk DCIS. In this commentary, we review the challenges of identifying patients with ADH at sufficiently low risk of upgrade and summarize emerging outcome data supporting active monitoring. We discuss the target trial emulation study by Rangel and colleagues, evaluating active monitoring versus surgical excision for selected patients with ADH, as well as novel tools that may further support this approach. Together, these developments suggest a growing role for individualized management strategies in ADH. See related article by Rangel et al., p. 577.

Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer. METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison. RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]). CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

title: Beyond Weight Loss: Rethinking Dietary and Lifestyle Interventions for Liver Disease Modification in MASLD.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is commonly managed with dietary and lifestyle intervention, and weight loss is often used as a key marker of treatment success. However, changes in body weight alone do not fully describe the effects of lifestyle intervention on liver disease. This narrative review asks when lifestyle-induced changes can support a claim of liver disease modification. Current guidance generally associates sustained weight loss of at least 5% with reduced liver fat, 7-10% with reduced liver inflammation, and at least 10% with improvement in fibrosis. The review distinguishes weight loss from biological response, pathological improvement, and long-term clinical benefit. It considers how intervention exposure, biological response, outcome type, and duration of follow-up should be interpreted together. It also addresses differences in patient response, long-term adherence, and the limits of different study designs. Randomized trials, long-term observational studies, and target-trial emulation are considered in relation to what they can establish about causality and long-term benefit. We propose a five-question framework for evaluating lifestyle-induced liver disease modification: Who? What? Through which pathway? What outcome? For how long and with what evidence? Weight loss remains an important treatment target, but it should not be considered synonymous with liver disease modification. Claims of disease modification should reflect the level of evidence available. This framework provides a clearer way to distinguish short-term improvement from meaningful and durable modification of MASLD.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Insulin Degludec Versus Insulin Glargine in Trial-Eligible and Ineligible Populations: A DEVOTE-Inspired Target Trial Emulation Using the Swedish National Diabetes Register.
abstract: AIMS: To compare cardiovascular outcomes associated with the initiation of insulin degludec versus insulin glargine using a target trial emulation approach in nationwide real-world data. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study using Swedish health registers, including the National Diabetes Register. Individuals with type 2 diabetes initiating insulin degludec or insulin glargine between 2012 and 2022 were included. Two complementary approaches were applied: a trial-eligible emulation cohort reflecting the eligibility criteria of the DEVOTE trial, and a trial-ineligible emulation cohort representing routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, i.e., myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular mortality). Secondary outcomes included the individual components of MACE, all-cause mortality and heart failure. Average treatment effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation. RESULTS: Among 96 731 individuals identified, 44 890 met the study eligibility criteria and were included in the analyses. In the trial-eligible cohort, degludec was associated with a similar risk of MACE compared with glargine (risk ratio: 1.10; 95% CI: 0.91-1.34; p = 0.34), but a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.92; p = 0.002). In the trial-ineligible emulation cohort, degludec was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.95; p = 0.004) as well as reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal stroke and heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study, degludec was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with glargine, consistently observed in both trial-eligible and trial-ineligible populations, despite similar cardiovascular risk in the trial-eligible cohort.

title: Causal Impact of Adherence to Canada’s Food Guide on Mortality, Life Expectancy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Target Trial Emulation With an Equity Lens
Combined statin and fenofibrate therapy and cardiorenal outcomes in patients with CKD, dyslipidemia, and ischemic heart disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults with non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and hypertriglyceridemia are at high cardiorenal risk; whether starting fenofibrate together with statin therapy is effective and safe in this population is uncertain. METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective cohort study emulating a target trial in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (2018-2024), 112 003 (28.5%) of 392 969 statin initiators with CKD and hypertriglyceridemia had IHD. Those without dialysis dependence were assigned to statin-fenofibrate combination therapy or statin monotherapy according to fenofibrate initiation within 3 months of the first statin prescription. The main outcomes were expanded major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) (acute myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, cardiac arrest, or all-cause death) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) necessitating dialysis. Propensity score matching yielded 3191 pairs. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs). RESULTS: Median follow-up was 881 days with combination therapy and 925 days with statin monotherapy. Combination therapy was associated with lower risks of MACE [1472 [46.1%] vs 1576 [49.4%] events; HR, 0.93; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.86-0.99] and ESKD necessitating dialysis (264 [8.3%] vs 335 [10.5%]; HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67-0.92). Risks of all-cause mortality (377 vs. 375), acute myocardial infarction (537 vs. 570), heart failure (1059 vs. 1134), stroke (310 vs. 312), acute kidney injury (825 vs. 840), and coded safety events were not significantly different between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among selected adults with non-dialysis-dependent CKD, hypertriglyceridemia, and IHD, statin-fenofibrate combination therapy was associated with lower risks of MACE and of ESKD necessitating dialysis, without a significant increase in coded safety events.

title: Comparative effectiveness of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole dosing strategies for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia: a target trial emulation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) is considered first-line therapy for Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP); however, dosing recommendations have remained largely unchanged since the 1970s. Current dosing may increase adverse effects without clear beneficial outcomes. This study evaluated the comparative effectiveness of high-, intermediate-, and low-dose TMP-SMX on short-term mortality. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study emulating a target trial using Epic Cosmos of adult patients with PCP who received initial TMP-SMX treatment from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2025. Patients were categorized into high (≥15 mg/kg/day), intermediate (10-15 mg/kg/day), or low dose (≤10 mg/kg/day) groups. Outcomes including 30-day mortality, 90-day mortality, and hyperkalemia (serum potassium ≥5.5 mmol/L) were assessed using propensity score overlap-weighted Cox models with multiple imputation to estimate missing variables. RESULTS: Among 4,572 patients, 2,348 (51.3%) received high-, 1,466 (32.1%) intermediate-, and 758 (16.6%) low-dose TMP-SMX. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 791 (17.3%) patients. After overlap weighting, low-dose (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.57-1.08; p=0.135) and intermediate-dose TMP-SMX (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.74-1.16; p=0.503) were not associated with mortality compared to high-dose TMP-SMX. Hyperkalemia occurred in 27.4% and was less frequent with low- (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.46-0.78; p<0.001) but not intermediate-dose therapy (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.72-1.02; p=0.085). CONCLUSIONS: TMP-SMX dose for PCP treatment was not associated with 30-day mortality after accounting for relevant clinical factors. Lower dosed TMP-SMX may be effective for PCP therapy with less hyperkalemia. Randomized trials are needed to confirm optimal PCP dosing strategies.

Denosumab Therapy Duration and Osteonecrosis of the Jaw and Skeletal Events in Bone-Metastatic Prostate Cancer.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Denosumab reduces skeletal-related events in bone-metastatic prostate cancer but carries a cumulative risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ). The treatment duration that best balances these risks has not been established in clinical settings. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between duration of denosumab treatment and the 3-year cumulative incidence of ONJ and skeletal events. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study emulated a target trial using Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service data from January 1, 2009, through August 31, 2024; patients were not randomized. A clone-censor-weight approach with inverse probability of censoring weighting estimated 3-year cumulative incidence and risk ratios (RRs), with death as a competing event. Men included in the analysis had bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and initiated oncologic-dose denosumab therapy; men with castration-sensitive disease were excluded. EXPOSURES: Six strategies defined by 3 durations (≤6, 7-12, and ≥13 months), each as a schedule-flexible group and a schedule-adherent subgroup (intervals ≤12 weeks). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Three-year cumulative incidence of ONJ and skeletal events (pathologic fracture, spinal cord compression, and surgery to bone) was the primary outcome; a radiotherapy-inclusive conventional composite of skeletal-related events was assessed as a secondary outcome. RESULTS: Among 3307 men included in the analysis (mean [SD] age, 72.6 [8.6] years; median follow-up, 42.6 [IQR, 26.5-57.4] months), the overall 3-year cumulative incidence was 9.8% (95% CI, 8.7%-11.0%) for ONJ and 4.9% (95% CI, 4.2%-5.7%) for skeletal events. Relative to treatment for 6 months or less, treatment for 7 to 12 months showed a lower risk of skeletal events (3.82% [95% CI, 3.04%-4.80%] vs 5.76% [95% CI, 4.23%-7.79%]; RR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.45-0.97]) and higher risk of ONJ (3.28% [95% CI, 2.41%-4.44%] vs 1.47% [95% CI, 0.86%-2.50%]; RR, 2.22 [95% CI, 1.21-4.11]). Compared with 7 to 12 months, treatment for 13 months or longer was associated with higher risk of ONJ (12.20% [95% CI, 10.86%-13.68%]; risk difference, 8.93 [95% CI, 7.16-10.64] percentage points), without further reduction in risk for skeletal events (3.99% [95% CI, 3.30%-4.82%]; risk difference, 0.17 [95% CI, -1.03 to 1.31] percentage points). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, denosumab treatment for 7 to 12 months was associated with lower risk of skeletal events and a modest increase in ONJ, whereas treatment beyond 12 months was associated with markedly higher ONJ risk but no further reduction of skeletal events. These findings support individualized reassessment of denosumab treatment duration after approximately 1 year.

title: Discontinuing Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Based Therapy After Complete Response in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Evidence, Bias, and a Research Framework.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens can induce radiographic complete response (CR) in a small but clinically important subset of patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Whether treatment can then be stopped safely remains unresolved. Evidence comes predominantly from retrospective cohorts and post hoc analyses: selected complete responders have durable disease control after cessation, but neither patient-selection criteria nor an optimal post-CR treatment duration has been validated. This structured critical narrative review distinguishes direct evidence in HCC complete responders from indirect HCC studies, local-treatment-assisted CR, and evidence from other tumors. Interpretation depends on the response criterion, confirmation of CR, reason for stopping, residual treatment exposure, and the alignment of treatment assignment with follow-up. Chronic liver disease adds competing mortality and can reduce the opportunity for salvage independently of tumor recurrence. We integrate these issues into a clinical assessment pathway and a framework for prospective research, with attention to recurrence phenotype, hepatic reserve, toxicity, treatment burden, and treatment-free outcomes. Priorities include reproducible CR definitions, longitudinal registries, comparisons of prespecified treatment strategies, and prospective evaluation of surveillance and salvage. Current evidence supports individualized discussion of cessation rather than its routine use after CR or a fixed treatment duration.

title: Early national comparison of robotic versus conventional knee replacements for arthritis using National Joint Registry data: target trial emulation study
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the early comparative effectiveness of robotic versus conventional total knee replacement (TKR) and unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) in the UK. Design Target trial emulation study. Setting Public and private hospitals using data from the National Joint Registry of England, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, Guernsey, and Jersey. Participants 697 145 knee replacement surgeries between 2018 and 2024: 675 034 were conventional (TKRs and UKRs) and 22 111 were robotic. Main outcome measures The main outcome was five year knee replacement survival (mean 2.5 years follow-up); all cause revision risk; cause specific revision risk; intraoperative complications; and revision complexity of robotic versus conventional (TKR and UKR) knee replacement. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses were used to compare implant survival and indications for revision surgery. Propensity score matching using target trial emulation framework was used to estimate the average treatment effect in the treated population. Results The five year implant survival of the matched conventional and robotic TKR groups was 98.5% (95% confidence interval (CI) 98.3% to 98.7%) and 98.6% (98.2% to 99.0%), respectively, with no between group difference in revision risk (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.26; P=0.71). The five year implant survival of the matched conventional and robotic UKR groups was 97.8% (95% CI 97.2% to 98.3%) and 96.4% (92.4% to 98.3%), respectively, with no between group difference in revision risk (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.42; P=0.86). Cause specific revision risk and intraoperative complication risks did not differ between groups for either TKR or UKR. Conclusions No statistically significant differences were detected in revision risk, cause specific risk, or intraoperative complication risk between the robotic and conventional groups. This was consistent for both TKR and UKR. The possibility of unmeasured and residual confounding cannot be ruled out, however, owing to the observational design of the study. These results highlight the importance of careful evaluation of robotic technology in publicly funded healthcare systems, given the substantially higher capital and procedural costs involved.

title: Early Nocturnal Care Disruption and the Hazard of Incident ICU Delirium in Critically Ill Adults: A Target-Trial Emulation in MIMIC-IV.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nighttime care contacts fragment sleep and are often invoked as a contributor to intensive care delirium. Whether a higher intensity of those contacts early in the stay is associated with later incident delirium is unclear. Sicker, more sedated patients are monitored more often overnight and are also more likely to become delirious. METHODS: We emulated a target trial in MIMIC-IV version 3.1. Adults were eligible if the first intensive care stay lasted at least 48 hours and the delirium screen was negative at that landmark. High exposure was a nocturnal contact rate above the cohort median, built from vital-sign charting, laboratory draws, and bedside medication administrations between 22:00 and 05:59 and divided by 16 nocturnal hours. Follow-up for incident delirium began at the landmark. We estimated the hazard ratio with stabilized inverse-probability weights and a pooled-logistic survival model. RESULTS: Of 12,922 eligible stays, 2,862 developed incident delirium. High nocturnal care-contact intensity was associated with a higher hazard (adjusted hazard ratio 1.43, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 1.60). The hazard rose across tertiles of the contact rate and was higher for vital-sign charting and phlebotomy than for medication administration. CONCLUSIONS: A higher intensity of early nocturnal care contacts was associated with a moderately higher hazard of incident delirium. Residual confounding remains possible, including reverse causation if prodromal delirium itself increases overnight contacts before the first positive screen.

title: Early versus deferred intravenous calcium in patients with sepsis and ionized hypocalcemia: a target-trial emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravenous calcium is frequently administered during sepsis, yet whether early treatment improves 24-h hemodynamic recovery remains uncertain. We compared 24-h hemodynamic recovery between calcium initiation within 2 h of a non-emergency low-ionized calcium (iCa) result and no calcium initiation during the first 6 h after the result. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of 2016-2025 high-resolution electronic health records from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital. Adults with sepsis, final or corrected iCa of 0.90-1.10 mmol/L, and no emergency indication were eligible at result availability. Strategies were executed calcium within 2 h versus no calcium through 6 h; care after 6 h was unrestricted. Clone-censor weighting and overlap tilting addressed grace periods, measured time-varying confounding, and clinical equipoise. The primary outcome was being alive and vasopressor-free at 24 h. Estimates and two-sided 95% percentile intervals came from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap samples with model refitting. RESULTS: Of 5,993 patients, 1,538 initiated calcium within 2 h, 147 initiated at 2-6 h, and 4,308 received none through 6 h; none of the latter initiated calcium during 6-24 h. The standardized probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery was 69.9% with early calcium and 61.1% with deferral, corresponding to a risk difference of + 8.69 percentage points (95% percentile interval, + 4.66 to + 12.84) and a risk ratio of 1.142 (1.074-1.214). The estimated association varied with baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose (Holm-adjusted P = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶), whereas the iCa interaction did not remain statistically supported after adjustment (P = 0.097). Early calcium was associated with a 1.29-percentage-point higher observed risk of hypercalcemia (95% percentile interval, + 0.64 to + 2.05). Intervals for severe arrhythmia, new renal replacement therapy, and hospital mortality included the null. CONCLUSIONS: Early intravenous calcium was associated with a higher probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery than the deferred strategy, whose observed pathway involved no calcium through 24 h. Estimated effects were larger at higher vasopressor doses. Early calcium was associated with a modestly higher observed risk of hypercalcemia. These findings support randomized evaluation in vasopressor-treated patients. Baseline iCa modification remains exploratory.

title: Evaluating Darbepoetin Treatment Strategies for Managing Anaemia in Haemodialysis Patients: Effects on All-Cause Mortality From a Target Trial Emulation Using Electronic Health Record Data.
abstract: PURPOSE: Anaemia is a common complication of chronic kidney disease, often treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs), but the optimal haemoglobin (Hb) target remains uncertain. Using electronic health records, we emulated a target trial comparing different Hb targets in haemodialysis patients to estimate their effects on mortality. METHODS: We used electronic health records from UK kidney centres reporting to the UK Renal Registry. Adults aged ≥ 18 years, receiving haemodialysis for ≥ 3 months, and without marked ESA resistance were eligible. Using the clone-censor-weight method, we emulated trials comparing Hb targets: (1) 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L and (2) 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L. Darbepoetin dosing followed a standardised protocol with predefined dose adjustments and a maximum dose of 150 μg/week. The outcome was all-cause mortality over 8 months. RESULTS: The study included 8628 patients from 10 centres between 2004 and 2016; 62% male, median age 66 years (IQR 52-76). At baseline, mean Hb was 97.7 g/L (SD 15.1), and 79% of patients were receiving darbepoetin. The hazard ratio for mortality was 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.12) for the 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L comparison, and 1.20 (95% CI 0.94-1.54) for the 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L comparison. Adherence to the highest Hb target was lower, limiting precision. CONCLUSIONS: Targeting an Hb range of 105-125 g/L under controlled ESA dosing was not associated with increased mortality compared with 95-115 g/L. Targeting Hb levels above 125 g/L may increase mortality risk, consistent with previous trial findings.

title: From Adipose Tissue Dysfunction to Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for venous thromboembolism (VTE), driven by adipose tissue dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, hypercoagulability, impaired fibrinolysis, immunothrombosis, and venous stasis. Modern incretin-based therapies induce substantial weight loss and improve multiple cardiometabolic abnormalities that may influence thrombotic risk. To critically evaluate the biological rationale and clinical evidence supporting a potential role of incretin-based therapies in modifying VTE risk, while distinguishing mechanistic plausibility from proven clinical benefit and weight-loss-mediated effects from direct pharmacological actions. Methods: Narrative review of MEDLINE/PubMed and EMBASE (2000-2026), with critical appraisal of mechanistic studies, randomized trials, pharmacoepidemiological evidence, and current clinical recommendations. Results: Experimental and translational studies provide biological plausibility for potential antithrombotic effects of incretin-based therapies through modulation of inflammation, endothelial function, platelet activation, and coagulation pathways; however, these biomarkers are not validated surrogate endpoints for VTE. An expanding body of contemporary observational evidence, including active-comparator studies and target-trial emulations, has generally reported lower rates of VTE, pulmonary embolism, and/or deep vein thrombosis among patients receiving incretin-based therapies, although effect estimates vary according to population, comparator, and clinical setting. In contrast, recent meta-analyses of randomized trials have not demonstrated a significant reduction in overall VTE and have yielded partly conflicting findings for pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis. Major cardiovascular outcome trials were not specifically designed or powered to assess VTE. Current evidence suggests that sustained weight loss is the most plausible mediator of any potential long-term reduction in VTE risk, whereas a clinically relevant weight-independent antithrombotic effect remains unproven. Conclusions: Incretin-based therapies have a compelling biological rationale and a growing observational signal for potential VTE risk reduction, but current evidence is insufficient to establish a causal protective effect. Any potential long-term benefit appears most plausibly related to sustained weight loss and reversal of obesity-associated prothrombotic abnormalities, while a clinically relevant weight-independent antithrombotic effect remains unproven. Accordingly, these therapies should continue to be prescribed according to established metabolic indications, and any reduction in VTE risk should be regarded as a potential but unconfirmed additional benefit. Dedicated randomized trials with prespecified and adjudicated VTE outcomes are required before VTE prevention can be considered a therapeutic indication.

title: From prediction to decision: prediction-based decision rules and target trial emulation in ADHD.
abstract: More than 100 prediction models have been developed to support the diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment of ADHD, yet none has reached routine clinical practice. In this Personal View, we argue that an important reason for this implementation gap is the absence of clearly defined prediction-based decision rules-formalised mappings from a model's output to specific clinical actions. Most published models report discrimination metrics such as the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve, but do not specify what a clinician should do differently for a patient classified as at high risk versus low risk. Without this link to action, even an accurate model remains clinically inert. We describe how prediction-based decision rules, combined with target trial emulation of their clinical utility in large observational datasets, offer a feasible path forward. We illustrate the approach with two worked ADHD examples (treatment intensity guided by predicted persistence and medication selection guided by predicted treatment response) and propose four priorities to shift the field from model development towards decision-oriented evaluation and implementation.

GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy and incident atrial fibrillation in non-diabetic adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease: a propensity matched cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are potent risk factors for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet whether GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) prevent incident AF in non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD is unexamined. We assessed whether GLP-1RA therapy reduces 1-year AF incidence in this cardiorenal phenotype. METHODS: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (66 healthcare organizations), we conducted a retrospective target trial emulation of non-diabetic adults aged 18 or older with obesity and CKD stages 3-5 diagnosed 2021-2024. Patients receiving semaglutide, liraglutide, or tirzepatide (n = 10,985) were compared with unexposed patients (n = 94,527). After propensity score matching, 7326 patients remained per cohort. The primary outcome was incident AF at 1 year; secondary outcomes included AF subtypes, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and all-cause hospitalization. Cox models generated hazard ratios (HRs); sensitivity analyses extended follow-up to 2-3 years with landmark analyses. RESULTS: At 1 year, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower incident AF (1.63% vs. 2.62%; HR 0.655, 95% CI 0.508-0.844; p = 0.001), a 34.5% relative risk reduction. Reductions were consistent for paroxysmal (HR 0.586), persistent (HR 0.482), and longstanding persistent AF (HR 0.527; all p < 0.05); permanent AF was non-significant at 1 year. Ventricular tachyarrhythmias (HR 0.556; p = 0.002) and hospitalization (HR 0.668; p < 0.001) were also significantly reduced. Benefits persisted across 2- and 3-year follow-up and remained consistent in landmark analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In non-diabetic adults with obesity and CKD, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significant, durable reductions in incident AF, ventricular arrhythmias, and hospitalization. These findings are consistent with a possible cardiorenal benefit and support prioritizing this phenotype for dedicated randomized trials.

Improving causal inference in neighbourhood-health research by applying target trial emulation to relocation data
abstract: Inferring causality is a major challenge for researchers interested in the health effects of neighbourhood environmental characteristics. The reliance on observational data in this research area comes with a risk of confounding and selection bias that threatens the validity of study findings and resulting policy and practice recommendations. The objective of this paper is to propose an approach that applies the target trial emulation framework to relocation data to avoid such biases. The approach is illustrated based on a study aiming to examine the causal effect of urban public park access on risk for major depressive disorder. The proposed approach can be applied to studies foreseeing novel data collection or studies using secondary data analyses. By applying target trial emulation to relocation data, neighbourhood-health studies will result in more valid and effective policy and practice recommendations to build healthy and sustainable neighbourhoods.

title: Induction of labour and developmental outcomes in children: protocol for a target trial emulation
abstract: We will use a target trial emulation applied to a population-wide administrative linked health and welfare dataset based in NSW Australia to ascertain if induction of labour adversely impacts on child development at school start (4-6 years of age).

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21]; P=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF. STUDY DESIGN: Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System. SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019). EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis. OUTCOMES: Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary). ANALYTICAL APPROACH: We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2. LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding. CONCLUSIONS: Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

title: Key safety outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors versus DPP-4 inhibitors in general and vulnerable participants with T2DM: A target trial emulation study.
abstract: AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), a class of oral hypoglycaemic agents (OHAs), have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits. However, safety concerns may hinder their broader adoption, particularly among frail populations. We evaluated key safety outcomes associated with SGLT2i compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4i), an OHA class with low risks of complications. METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation (TTE) study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) and enrolled participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Eligible participants were categorized according to newly initiated SGLT2i (n = 224,510) or newly initiated DPP4i (n = 698,012) with continuous use for at least 30 days. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the SGLT2i group showed significantly lower incidence rate (per person-years) of several safety outcomes than the DPP4i group, including urinary tract infection (UTI) (23.84‰ vs. 27.88‰; hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.84-0.87), fractures or falls (16.55‰ vs. 17.79‰; HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.91-0.95), acute kidney injury (AKI) (1.06‰ vs. 1.91‰; HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.51-0.59), bullous pemphigoid (0.02‰ vs. 0.07‰; HR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.23-0.54), and all-cause mortality (13.05‰ vs. 19.72‰; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.65-0.67). Conversely, the risk of genital infection was higher in the SGLT2i group (2.96‰ vs. 2.05‰; HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.38-1.51). These findings remained consistent in the per-protocol analysis, across most vulnerable subgroups and individual SGLT2i and DPP4i agents. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i, compared with DPP4i, demonstrated a favourable safety profile across most evaluated outcomes, except for genital infections.

title: LLM-Driven Target Trial Emulation with Human-in-the-Loop Validation for Randomized Trial: Automated Protocol Extraction and Real-World Outcome Evaluation{Psi}
abstract: Target trial emulation (TTE) enables causal inference from observational data but remains bottlenecked by manual, expert-dependent protocol operationalization. While large language models (LLMs) have advanced clinical knowledge extraction and code generation, their ability to automate end-to-end TTE workflows remains largely unexplored. We present an LLM-driven framework using retrieval-augmented generation to extract the five core TTE design parameters from the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trial (CREST-2) protocol and generate executable phenotyping pipelines for real-world EHR data. The performance of the framework was evaluated along two dimensions. First, protocol extraction accuracy was assessed against a gold-standard checklist of trial design components using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Second, outcome validity was evaluated through population-level concordance analyses comparing EHR-derived outcomes with published trial endpoints using standardized mean difference, observed-to-expected ratios, confidence interval overlap, and two-proportion z-tests. Further, Human-in-the-loop validation assessed the correctness of extracted clinical logic and phenotype definitions. Together, these evaluations demonstrate a structured approach for assessing LLM-driven protocol-to-pipeline translation for scalable real-world evidence generation.

title: Metabolic bariatric surgery versus GLP-1 receptor agonists in dialysis patients with diabetes and obesity: a target trial emulation study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes, but their comparative survival and waitlisting benefits in end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: To compare survival and kidney transplant (KT) waitlisting after MBS and GLP-1RA use among patients with ESKD, using dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) as an active comparator. SETTING: US Renal Data System, 2010-2022. METHODS: We included adults with ESKD, type 2 diabetes, and ≥class II obesity treated with MBS, GLP-1RA, or DPP-4i. Three target trials were emulated: MBS versus GLP-1RA (N = 1818), MBS versus DPP-4i (N = 2111), and GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i (N = 4338). Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for all-cause mortality and KT waitlisting over 1-5 years. RESULTS: MBS recipients were younger at dialysis initiation than matched GLP-1RA and DPP-4i users. MBS was associated with higher short-term mortality than matched GLP-1RA (1-year aHR = 2.68, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.98-3.63; 3-year aHR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.09-1.64) and DPP-4i users (1-year aHR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.35-2.25), but comparable longer-term mortality. GLP-1RA users had consistently lower mortality than matched DPP-4i users. MBS was associated with higher KT waitlisting than GLP-1RA and DPP-4i use, with no differences between GLP-1RA and DPP-4i users. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ESKD, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, MBS was associated with higher short-term but comparable long-term mortality, whereas GLP-1RA use was associated with lower mortality than DPP-4i use. MBS was also associated with higher KT waitlisting than GLP-1RA and DPP-4i use, suggesting distinct risk-benefit profiles of metabolic treatment in this high-risk population.

title: On estimands in target trial emulation
abstract: The target trial framework enables causal inference from longitudinal observational data by emulating randomized trials initiated at multiple time points. Precision is often improved by pooling information across trials, with standard models typically assuming - among other things - a time-constant treatment effect. However, this obscures interpretation when the true treatment effect varies, which we argue to be likely as a result of relying on noncollapsible estimands. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a model-free strategy for target trial analysis, centered around the choice of the estimand, rather than model specification. This ensures that treatment effects remain clearly interpretable for well-defined populations even under model misspecification. We propose estimands suitable for different study designs, and develop accompanying G-computation and inverse probability weighted estimators. Applications on simulations and real data on antimicrobial de-escalation in an intensive care unit setting demonstrate the greater clarity and reliability of the proposed methodology over traditional techniques.

title: Open- versus closed-cell stents in transfemoral carotid artery stenting for carotid bifurcation disease: a target trial emulation.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE
The comparative association of open-cell and closed-cell stent design with outcomes after protected transfemoral carotid artery stenting, particularly long-term patency, remains uncertain. This study compared open-cell and closed-cell stents in patients with carotid bifurcation disease.


METHODS
We retrospectively emulated a target trial using data from three centers. Consecutive patients who underwent transfemoral carotid artery stenting with embolic protection devices for atherosclerotic carotid bifurcation lesions were included and classified according to stent design. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Periprocedural outcomes were assessed within 30 days. Follow-up outcomes included in-stent restenosis, severe in-stent restenosis, symptomatic in-stent restenosis, recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (stroke or transient ischemic attack), and target-vessel revascularization.


RESULTS
Among 1024 patients, 524 (51.2%) were symptomatic and 500 (48.8%) were asymptomatic; 577 received open-cell stents and 447 received closed-cell stents. Median follow-up was 26.0 months (interquartile range, 19.4-32.4 months). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Periprocedural adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. During follow-up, closed-cell stent use was associated with higher risks of in-stent restenosis (hazard ratio, 1.66; 95% confidence interval, 1.19-2.31; P = .003), severe in-stent restenosis (hazard ratio, 1.61; 95% confidence interval, 1.06-2.45; P = .026), symptomatic in-stent restenosis (hazard ratio, 2.03; 95% confidence interval, 1.20-3.45; P = .008), and recurrent transient ischemic attack (hazard ratio, 3.06; 95% confidence interval, 1.24-7.55; P = .015). Any in-stent restenosis and severe in-stent restenosis were strongly associated with recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (both P < .001). Closed-cell stent use appeared more strongly associated with in-stent restenosis in symptomatic patients, without significant interaction by symptom status (P for interaction = .206). Sensitivity analyses were concordant with the primary results.


CONCLUSIONS
Open-cell stents were associated with a lower hazard of restenosis and no material difference in periprocedural outcomes compared with closed-cell stents. These findings support preferential consideration of open-cell stents at the carotid bifurcation for long-term patency, while closed-cell stents may retain a theoretical advantage in unstable plaques requiring denser plaque coverage.

title: Partitioning Time in Target Trial Emulation
abstract: In target trial emulation, the treatment strategies that patients follow are inferred from the treatments they actually receive in routine care. However, in most settings, the outcome may preclude the observation of planned treatment, giving rise to immortal time bias through misclassification of treatment strategy, while markers of treatment response may influence subsequent treatment decisions, giving rise to time-varying confounding. A key step toward unbiased treatment effect estimation is to partition follow-up into sufficiently short time intervals to unfold the feedback relationships involving treatment and represent the resulting causal relations with a directed acyclic graph. In this study, we present the possible within-interval causal orderings induced by this partitioning, discuss their causal implications, and assess their plausibility across clinical settings. For each causal ordering, we derive the corresponding g-formula. Using ancestral multi-world networks and simulations, we show that the standard cloning-censoring-weighting estimator is invalid when treatment affects the outcome within a time interval, and we propose a modified version of the method that restores its validity in this setting. Finally, we analyze the consequences of choosing time intervals that are either excessively wide or excessively narrow, thereby formally establishing the need for time partitioning and providing practical guidance for selecting an appropriate partition based on the clinical setting.

title: Pectoral-branch entry-point anatomy and a standardised skeletonisation workflow for the pectoralis major island flap: an anatomical description and observational clinical analysis in adult chinese males.
abstract: PURPOSE: To define the most distal entry point (MDEP) of the pectoral branch in adult Chinese males, integrate it into a standardised Landmark-Axis-Plane (LAP) skeletonisation workflow for the pectoralis major island flap, and describe its clinical performance under IDEAL Stage 2a. METHODS: The anatomical phase measured the MDEP in 20 formalin-fixed adult Chinese male cadavers (40 hemithoraces). The clinical phase analysed 194 males (skeletonised, n = 74; conventional, n = 120) treated contemporaneously by two surgical teams at a single centre using a target trial emulation framework with propensity-score overlap weighting and logistic regression with robust sandwich variance estimation. The primary endpoint was 30-day Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III complications. The technique and team were strictly collinear; all estimates are noncausal. RESULTS: The MDEP lay 6.2-6.5 cm below the midclavicular point, predominantly at the third rib or third intercostal space. Severe complications occurred in 5 of 74 (6.8%) skeletonised patients versus 27 of 120 (22.5%) conventional patients (weighted OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.10-0.78, P = 0.016); flap necrosis was also lower (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.03-0.58). E-value analysis indicated that the primary association is vulnerable to moderate unmeasured confounding. QuickDASH data are descriptive only (62.8% of non-responders had died). CONCLUSION: The MDEP provides a reproducible bony-landmark reference for pedicle skeletonisation in adult Chinese males. The LAP workflow was associated with fewer severe complications, but strict technique-team collinearity and sensitivity to unmeasured confounding preclude a causal interpretation. Multicentre IDEAL Stage 2b validation is required.

title: Physical activity and combinations with modifiable factors and risk of cognitive impairment: the Whitehall II study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Physical activity is a key modifiable protective factor for cognitive health, but randomized controlled trials initiating physical activity in late life have often failed to demonstrate significant cognitive benefits. The optimal window for prevention may be midlife, before irreversible pathology is established. We emulated a target trial to estimate counterfactual risks of cognitive impairment under hypothetical strategies of initiating or maintaining physical activity, alone or in combination with lifestyle and vascular risk modifications from midlife. METHODS: We utilized data from the Whitehall II study (n = 3011) with baseline ages 45 to 64, following participants from midlife for up to 18 years. We applied the parametric g-formula to handle time-varying confounding and emulate hypothetical interventions. Strategies included physical activity, alone or combined with modifications to diet, smoking, alcohol consumption, and vascular risk modification (systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol, fasting glucose, and body mass index). The primary outcome was cognitive impairment based on cognitive tests. One thousand sets of bootstrapping were conducted to obtain 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Initiating physical activity alone did not significantly reduce the 18-year cumulative incidence of cognitive impairment. However, the estimated risk of cognitive impairment was lower under the strategy combining physical activity with healthy diet and no smoking, and with normal body mass index, compared with the natural course. Also, comprehensive strategies targeting physical activity, lifestyle factors, and all vascular risk factors achieved significant risk reduction. DISCUSSION: While physical activity initiated in midlife may be insufficient as a single intervention in this cohort, its integration into a comprehensive multidomain strategy addressing lifestyle and vascular health significantly reduces the risk of cognitive impairment. These findings support holistic prevention strategies from midlife to improve long-term cognitive outcomes.

Real-world effectiveness of monoclonal antibody lecanemab versus acetylcholinesterase inhibitors in Alzheimer's disease: a target trial emulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND
Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEIs) provide symptomatic relief in Alzheimer's disease (AD), whereas lecanemab may modify disease progression; however, real-world evidence on its safety and clinical impact remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the safety and effectiveness of initiating lecanemab versus AChEIs in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD.


METHODS
Using the TriNetX US electronic health record network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study including individuals diagnosed with MCI or AD between July 2023 and September 2025. A target trial emulation with 1:1 propensity score matching and Cox models estimated comparative risks.


RESULTS
Lecanemab was associated with a fivefold higher incidence of neuroimaging abnormalities than AChEIs, while 1-year treatment persistence was similar (53.4% vs 52.5%). After matching, 589 patients were included in each cohort. Compared with AChEIs, lecanemab was associated with significantly lower risks of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) (HR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.36-0.77) and emergency visits (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85), but a higher risk of hospitalization (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.03-1.67). Lecanemab was also associated with lower use of antipsychotics (HR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.32-0.70), antidepressants (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85), melatonin/orexin antagonists (HR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.42-0.88), antibiotics (HR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.44-0.86), and antifungals (HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), whereas steroid use was higher among lecanemab users (HR, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.55-3.10).


CONCLUSIONS
Compared with an AChEI-based conventional care strategy, lecanemab initiation was associated with comparable treatment persistence and lower observed risks of BPSD, emergency visit as well as reduced use of psychotropic and infection-related medications in exploratory analyses. However, the higher incidence of neuroimaging abnormalities associated with lecanemab, along with increased risks of hospitalization and corticosteroid use, likely reflects proactive clinical monitoring and management of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). While residual confounding cannot be excluded and results warrant cautious interpretation, these exploratory findings warrant further validation in biomarker-confirmed cohorts and head-to-head randomized trials.

title: Reno-protective effects of statins among patients with chronic kidney disease in Hong Kong: a target trial emulation
abstract: Summary Background Many existing randomised controlled trials lack sufficient power to assess primary kidney outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether statin therapy offers a clinically meaningful reno-protective effect in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods In this retrospective cohort study, electronic health records in Hong Kong were extracted to perform sequential target trial emulation. Eligible adults (aged 18+ years) with CKD who met the indication for statin initiation between Jan 1, 2008 and Dec 31, 2017 were included; those with history of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded. Participants were categorised as statin initiators or non-initiators at each calendar month during inclusion period, where statin initiators were propensity score-matched with non-initiators. Follow-up data were collected for all participants until the occurrence of outcomes, death, loss to follow-up (2 years after last records), or the end of data availability (Dec 31, 2022), whichever occurred first. The hazard ratio (HR) of all-cause mortality, eGFR deterioration (eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2, ≥30% eGFR decline, and ≥50% eGFR decline) and composite outcomes (all-cause mortality, eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2, and ≥50% eGFR decline) was estimated by pooled logistic regression using intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) approach. Findings 1,437,014 eligible person-trials were identified (statin initiators n = 30,907; non-initiators n = 1,406,107), from which 30,892 statin initiators and 108,380 non-initiators were included after propensity-score matching. Relative to non-initiators, significant risk reduction was found among statin initiators in all-cause mortality (HR [95% confidence interval (CI)], ITT: 0.97 [0.95–0.98]; PP: 0.91 [0.88–0.93]), progression to eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 (ITT: 0.91 [0.89–0.93]; PP: 0.77 [0.74–0.80]), ≥50% eGFR decline (ITT: 0.95 [0.93–0.98]; PP: 0.89 [0.84–0.93]), and composite outcomes (ITT: 0.96 [0.94–0.97]; PP: 0.90 [0.88–0.92]). Statin therapy initiation was also associated significantly with reduced risk of ≥30% eGFR decline using PP approach (0.94 [0.92–0.96]). Interpretation Over a 10-year follow-up period, initiating statin therapy in patients with CKD was associated with a small yet significant decrease in all-cause mortality and a modest reno-protective effect. Future research should aim to clarify the effects of statin intensity, duration, and adherence. Funding National Natural Science Foundation of China.

abstract: KEY POINTS: Unknown if addition of newer diabetes medications is associated with kidney disease among older patients who were under recruited in clinical trials. In this target trial emulation, we report a protective association for kidney events and death for both glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor. The association of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor on kidney disease extended across multiple subgroups including short duration of use and in the older population. BACKGROUND: A trial emulation approach evaluated kidney outcomes for addition of three diabetes medications among Veterans, including older Veterans underrepresented in trials. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of Veterans with diabetes who were new users adding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), or dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is). Each group was followed until a composite of death or kidney event defined as a 50% decline in eGFR, kidney failure (transplant or dialysis) or censored for nonpersistence of drug class, loss of follow-up, and study end. The primary analysis used propensity score weights to compare the hazard of the composite outcome. The secondary analysis considered cause-specific hazard of kidney events with death as censoring. An Aalen-Johansen plot displayed individual outcomes of kidney event or death as a competing risk. Subgroup analyses evaluated Veterans by duration of use, age, eGFR, and urine protein. RESULTS: After propensity score weighting, the cohort included 42,684 GLP-1 RA, 44,198 SGLT2i, and 44,213 DPP4i episodes. The median age was 69 years, diabetes duration was 10.6 years (6.8-15.2), and eGFR was 75 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 (58-92). Event rates per 1000 person-years were 34.6 (33.3-36.0) versus 29.0 (27.8-30.3) versus 47.4 (46.0-48.9) for GLP-1 RA, SGLT2i, and DPP4i, respectively. There was a protective association for composite of kidney event and death for GLP-1 RA, hazard ratio (HR) 0.70 (0.67 to 0.74), and SGLT2i users (HR, 0.65 [0.61 to 0.68]) versus DPP4i. The results were similar for the cause-specific hazard of kidney event alone GLP-1 RA (HR, 0.72 [0.65 to 0.80]) and SGLT2i (HR, 0.48 [0.43 to 0.55]) and for subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RA and SGLT2i as add-on diabetes treatment were associated with lower composite and individual outcomes of kidney event and death. The association was similar across subgroups highlighting the value in primary prevention among older populations.

abstract: Tavoitekokeen jäljittely on lääketieteellisissä havainnoivissa tutkimuksissa yleistyvä menetelmä. Tavoitekokeen jäljittelyä käytetään viitekehyksenä havainnoivien tutkimusten suunnitteluun harhan välttämisen vuoksi. Työn tutkimuskysymys oli "Miten tavoitekokeen jäljittelyä voi parantaa ja soveltaa lääketieteessä?". Tämän työn tarkoitus oli täydentää puutteellista suomenkielistä kirjallisuutta tavoitekokeen jäljittelystä, ehdottaa mahdollisia parannuksia tavoitekokeen jäljittelyn käyttöön sekä tarkastella tutkimuskohteita, joihin tavoitekokeen jäljittelyä voisi soveltaa tulevaisuudessa. Työ toteutettiin kirjallisuuskatsauksena. Työssä todettiin tavoitekokeen jäljittelyn käytön vaativan standardisointia erityisesti tavoitekoeprotokollan käytössä ja nollahetken määrittämisessä. Havaittiin myös tarve uusille ja tehokkaammille tilastollisille työkaluille tukemaan tavoitekokeen jäljittelyä. Lisäksi saatiin selville, että havainnoivien aineistojen puutteellisuus on merkittävä tekijä tavoitekokeen jäljittelyn rajoituksissa. Tavoitekokeen jäljittelyn parantamista varten vaaditaan laajempia ja tarkempia havainnoivia aineistoja sekä uusia työkaluja. On myös tärkeää, että tavoitekokeen jäljittelyä käyttävät tutkimukset raportoivat käytetyt menetelmät sekä määrittävät tavoitekoeprotokollan ja nollahetken tarkasti. Tavoitekokeen jäljittely on lupaava menetelmä havainnoivien tutkimusten suunnittelussa. Menetelmä on kuitenkin uusi ja vaatii enemmän tutkimusta.

title: Target trial emulation and dynamic treatment strategies during endovascular thrombectomy.
Target trial emulation studies in oncology: a comprehensive analysis.
abstract: Background Target trial emulation (TTE) has emerged as an important framework for generating comparative effectiveness real-world evidence. However, the methodological characteristics and clinical utility of this framework in oncology remain insufficiently characterized. This study systematically evaluated the characteristics of oncological emulation studies. Materials and methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science Core Collection databases from inception to December 22, 2023, to identify oncology-focused TTE studies. Study characteristics, TTE components, and consistency with corresponding randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were analyzed. Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies and percentages and compared using Chi-square tests in SPSS (version 27.0), with P-values Results A total of 54 TTEs were included. Most were conducted in the United States (22, 40.7%), and publications peaked in 2023 (17, 31.5%). Colorectal cancer (13, 24.1%) was the most frequently investigated cancer type. Studies predominantly used data from national databases (18, 33.3%). While all studies prospectively specified the target trial protocol and emulation procedures, only 1 (1.9%) study was prospectively registered, and most emulation studies (48, 88.9%) did not reference a reporting guideline. Among the 10 RCT-TTE pairs available for comparison, 6 (60.0%) pairs achieved agreement in both statistical significance and effect estimates. Conclusion This study provides a comprehensive analysis of TTE studies in oncology, highlighting their value for generating higher-quality real-world evidence. Future efforts should prioritize prospective protocol registration and standardize reporting to enhance the credibility and reproducibility of emulation studies.
